Perfume rating 4.23 out of 5 with 5,921 votes

L'Instant Magic by Guerlain is a Floral Woody Musk fragrance for women. L'Instant Magic was launched in 2007. L'Instant Magic was created by Sylvaine Delacourte and Randa Hammami. Top notes are Anise, Bergamot and Lemon; middle notes are Violet, Mimosa, Rose, Freesia and Carnation; base notes are Almond, Iris, Vanilla, White Musk, Sandalwood and Cedar.

In September 2007, Guerlain launched L'Instant Magic, this time as Eau de Parfum and Parfum (regular version), together with a range of additional products. The fragrance features floral, woody and musk notes. There is bergamot in the top, rose and freesia in the heart and white musk in the base. The perfume was created by Randa Hammami of Symrise, 2007. It comes as EDP in 30 ml, 50m l and 80 ml bottles, and as concentrated Perfume in a 7.5 ml bottle.

Einfinken 09/17/23 03:16

This has been my signature winter scent for years now and I have gone through multiple bottles at this point.

This is a perfume that makes me feel like I am sitting under a freshly washed duvet and eating an almond croissant while watching the snow fall. If you are not a fan of almond or powdery scents this won't be for you, but I absolutely love it and it tends to be a compliment getter when I wear it (particularly from other women). More importantly, I feel fresh, clean, comfortable and uplifted when I wear this. Perhaps it is the lemon and bergamot that give this scent a cheery sort of vibe? Overall, I would say this is a scent for a grown woman, but it also isn't old fashioned or overly mature in my opinion. It's appropriate for almost any situation in the fall/winter, though it is much too much for spring or summer, in my opinion. Still, L'Instant Magic is one of my all-time favorite powdered almond scents and I am always excited when the weather starts getting colder and I know I can wear this again.

ETA: I see this has been reformulated and that's an absolute shame because the new version is not really the same as the bottle I have/reviewed above.

talkaboutscents 04/06/23 08:31

As a guy I think this "genre" of violet-musk powdery perfumes is just the classiest. L'Instant Magic is no exception. Since the release of Armani Lei in 1998 I became addicted to these powdery formulas, and thousands of perfumes later my opinions are the same. The reviewer below is spot on, that this is just a success-proven formula, be it Armani Lei for more fresh touches, Massimo Dutti's Souffle Marais (though short-lived and almost impossible to find nowadays), Lancome's discontinued Iris Dragees, Victoria Secret - Heavenly/Dream Angels Heavenly and less but still in the genre Prada Infusion d'Iris and Prada Candy...the list can go on as there are some celebrity fragrances that smells like that too, it takes me back to 90s and giving me all the classy/down to earth vibes when I smell it on a woman.

These are mentioned as "iris" scents but truly they are just violets fantasy creations and most times not iris. Even though both notes in the perfume marketing became almost interchangeable, in reality true-to-iris use is what you smell in Prada Iris. There's much more powder/violet ingredients (ionones) and musks than iris here, and touch of vanilla/coumarin (tonka) and sometimes combined with benzoin (as in Prada Candy). Often you start from the mid-base notes skipping all the top ones as they rarely come topped with citruses/fruits. And often it feels like they remain close to skin but in reality the diffusion of these scents are so good, it's a pleasure for people around. Comforting, clean, sexy, mild but recognizable, classy.

Perpetual Collector 05/19/22 11:50

I've owned both L'Instant Magic and L'Instant EDP for a few years now, both are old versions. I didn't wear them much, but after trying Keiko Mecheri Loukhoum, I got hooked on powdery stuff big time. So for the past week, I have been wearing these two versions of L'Instant intermittently, and I can finally tell apart the two. I am not going to dissect the L'Instant EDP here, but Magic is definitely lighter, deeper, and more sophisticated, if that is even possible, since, at least for me, the entire Guerlain lineup is ultra-sophisticated as it is. Could be due to added Lemon note but I can't tell for sure.
I adore both, but Magic has my heart. It's definitely longer lasting out of the two. I have struggled with original L'Instant's staying power since the early beginnings, but I can rarely get more than 3-4 hours out of it.
As things are standing right now, I prefer the Magic. I just landed the ultra-rare Magic Elixir, but didn't receive it yet, however, I can't wait to test that one as well. I think I want every single version of this, it's that good. As a side note, do not pass Keiko's Loukhoum because you have this, they are in the same vein, but not the same. Loukhoum is ultra edible and sexy, whereas L'Instant is a bit more classy and maybe a tad more serious. Loukhoum is really, really super good, so don't pass on it!

I have the original style bottle (shown in this page). From what I've read, the newest "candle" style bottle that is currently available is faithful to the original juice, though I have not tried it myself to compare.

Goodness - this is excellent! As a huge fan of Guerlain fragrances and powdery scents in general, I knew this would be a safe blind buy for me. In fact, it's quickly made itself comfortable in my list of all-time favorite fragrances!

L'Instant Magic (not to be confused with the singular "L'Instant") boasts a creamy rendition of powder, much like a high-end body cream. Those looking for a light, airy powder may be disappointed. This is smooth, sweet, and comforting with a well-blended floral bouquet, velvety vanilla, and dreamy musky background - but what really sets LM apart from my other powdery fragrances is the sense of depth I get from the rich cedar and almond. These denser woody notes merge beautifully with the lighter florals and powder, creating a feeling of hypnotic sensuality that borders on the soporific. The longevity and sillage are also excellent; I apply this before bed and am greeted in the morning by creamy vanilla powder and musk.

L'Instant Magic is beautiful, surprisingly rich, and very Guerlain. A new favorite!

White musk, mimosa and carnation stand out here with the slightest hint of vanilla. L'Instant Magic is a very soft, slightly powdery scent that is simple but well blended. It is different to the usual Guerlain signature iris dominant scents, although this note lingers in the background. While it is a fine powdery scent (not so thick as Chanel no. 5) it is not strongly reminiscent of baby powder or lotion to me; it just has the sweet softness people associate with innocence & simplicity. It is unique and comforting, enough to wear before bed, while still being sophisticated. L'Instant Magic is delicate, not sugary or headache inducing, and would be impossible to overspray. It is extremely calming - a happy, contented, dreamy and subtle scent that I enjoy wearing and very unthreatening, without being bland, to those around you. To me, this is the parallel mood to Apres L'Ondee, which I also own, the latter reflecting more serious, mature, reflective moments. I enjoy having both in my collection but I will wear the uplifting l'Instant Magic more frequently. While the sillage is low, the longevity is intermittent but generally good - others, as well as me, could still smell this on my wrist the following day. A truly beautiful scent.

jæ 05/23/20 16:22

Yeah, I get why people associate this with baby powder, mineral oil, lotion, and laundry products. The violet, sweet almond, iris, and freesia notes occur in many other household items we want to associate with cleanliness, warmth, and comfort. To me, this is not a disqualifier. L'Instant magique is more complex than any of these products, and more nuanced.

At first, the powdery iris and violet dance with the bright citruses and anise, which provides an almost licorice-like harmony. Soon, that beautiful vanilla-almond accord starts to come through, along with a host of other florals, which are difficult to detect individually. The breezy, nectar-sweet freesia is definitely there, as is the soapy rose, and maybe a hint of mimosa in all its pollinated glory. The drydown leads to an almond-musk-violet haze with flashes of flowers and anise.

Taken together, this is supremely refreshing and sheer, but melds very well with skin and sweat. The performance is middling, but this is one of those fragrances that is difficult to over-apply. At worst, you're left smelling like you've just bathed in a tub full of luscious soaps and oils, followed by the application of a fine lotion or body oil.

I should also note that this review is for the bee bottle version; I've never smelled earlier formulations. Traditionally feminine, but I wish more guys smelled this good and clean, haha. All-season, but blooms better in warm weather. Merci, Guerlain!

Dessert Powder

The lovely and innocent L'Instant Magic, so simple, comforting, and soft.

I am really becoming aware that Guerlain has to put dessert/gourmand notes in almost everything they do, as a house, and L'IM is no exception.

The predominant note here, make no exception, is powder. POWDER! In fact when I put it on my husband immediately commented, not meanly, "Did you put a bunch of baby powder on?"

I'd rather think that this is some sort of fantastical kitchen powder though used for desserts. To me the powder smells like sugared vanilla almond powder, with the barest hints of citrus in the top notes, then a sweet underlying floral mimosa in the middle, and as the base emerges a hint of darkened sandalwood, musk, and cedar. (I for one can hardly smell any iris, except maybe at the beginning.)

There are just hints of other things though, like I said this is mostly a powder scent. It has a emotional feel of wearing a clean, soft blanket, being warm and safe, being loved and happy. L'IM is very linear but it immerses you in a good feeling and I like that a lot.

That, and practically speaking this is a "SFW" scent and nowadays that's not a bad thing, to have something to wear that won't challenge anyone, and if accused to being perfumed you can just say that you put on baby powder after your shower that morning.

dsty 03/05/18 22:08

I love almond scents, and so it comes as no surprise that I also really like l'Instant Magic, which is a good representative of the category.

Firstly, and most importantly, the almond note is really well done here - it smells like marzipan without going overboard on the sweetness, which is exactly what I want from an almond scent. There is something just a little synthetic about it, but that seems to be hard to avoid with this note, and l'Instant Magic is better than most in that regard, so it's easy to forgive.
Otherwise, it's less bold than most almond fragrances I've tried before - instead of leaning heavily towards gourmand territory or being very powdery, this one has a soft, rather floral feeling to it, even a little soapy at times. Maybe just a little too subtle for my own personal taste, but very nice, and it also means it's more appropriate for year-round use.

All in all this is not my absolute favourite from this category, and not a hundred percent my thing, although I do really like it. Which means I'll probably stick with my small decant and be content with that - probably a blessing, if this has really been discontinued.

NixNox 01/02/18 07:37

I've held off from writing this review for some time - this perfume is so comforting and wonderful to me that I wasn't sure what to write about it. It's not a rational admiration or interest, here; it's pure emotional reaction and thus difficult to describe. First, a note on performance: this perfume has excellent longevity and moderate sillage. It certainly isn't 'soft' or negligible in terms of performance. You will carry the scent on your body all day, but in a fluffy cloud around you. You can detect all the notes within an arm's distance, but won't be blasting any rooms out. This is good because, overplayed, some of the notes here could be overpowering. Instead, the blend is perfect.

The first notes for me are green florals, sandalwood and marzipan. The iris, woods and almonds just sing together. It is soft and powdery - there is nothing shouting here - it's just a beautiful symphony of blended notes. The sweetness of the marzipan is tempered by the dry, cosy woods, and then the slightly bitter green note, which I think may be the combination of almond and iris. On dry-down, the iris becomes softer and more powdery, the almond remains sweet and edible throughout without ever being cloying, and the sandalwood is a sexy, comforting anchor.

Never underestimate the quiet ones - still waters run deep. This is the best almond perfume out there. The blend is masterful.

vonnnie 05/27/17 20:09

TLDR: Guerlain's fragrance game is weak here.
The reason I purchased a sample of L'Instant Magic is Randa Hammami, the perfumer who also created Mon Precieux Nectar extrait, that discontinued bitter almond, bergamot, vanilla and white musk blanket that makes me feel as delicious as a French confection. Some blogger mentioned a similarity. I can assure you with absolutely no doubt: there is none.
The most prominent top note is one I have also found in Versace Crystal Noir, Perris Monte Carlo Ylang Ylang Nosy Be EDT, and some designer men's colognes. It spoofs a warm, sort of vaguely citrus feeling and is blatantly synthetic to my nose. The rest of the pyramid is weak and powdery.

The blogger was Monsieur Guerlain. Monsieur, how could you betray me!?

"When Randa Hammami was commissioned to make a L'Instant Magic, only loosely related to L'Instant, she got the idea to infuse an overdose of white musks into some of Guerlain's finest players, bergamot, rose, sandalwood and bitter almond, the latter smelling somewhere between marzipan, cherry brandy and roasted nuts. The result combined the chewy taste of an amaretto macaron with a weightless, sensual silk-gown smoothness, so uniquely attractive as to be appointed new Guerlain signature. "I have nicknamed it the Musquinade in a playful reference to the Guerlinade," said Sylvaine Delacourte, "because both have this typical Guerlain DNA, which means an audacious overdose of certain raw materials, very beautiful natural ingredients that confer a signature, and a trail that is immediately recognizable."

Moral: While it's okay to let marketing develop an idea, it's unwise to allow them complete ownership over the perfume development (looking at you, Sylvaine Delacourte). It is a travesty to use "chewy" and "audacious overdose of raw materials" to describe whatever the fuck this is.
Summary: about the same level of magic as instant coffee. Guerlain needs to stealth it off the shelves, do a Nombre Noir landfill on this sucker, and let Thierry and Delphine have a go at rehabbing it. Since they would be turning lead into gold, call it L'Instant Alchemy.

At first I was disappointed but the more I wore it the more it grew on me. I thought initially it was too weak - for a Guerlain, anyway -, but while it is a very discreet one, it's always there, lasting throughout the day, always comforting and making me want to smell myself. That L'Instant Magic doesn't ever "try to hard" is part of it's charm.

It is definitely softer, less "edible", more clean smelling than something like Mondorlo di Sicilia by Acqua di Parma, which always brings to mind delicious French pastries. synergypsy 09/27/14 13:32

Just gorgeous! A classic, without a doubt.

Although overall a powdery fragrance, LIM is very complex and so well-blended I'm totally fascinated, and mystified at the same time. That's the "magic" part I guess! This fragrance wafts. Don't know how else to put it. It's waves of delightful fragrance impressions, yet never muddled, but softly purposeful, extremely well-balanced. Femininely rounded, in perfect harmony at all times.

Opens with soft citrus notes spiked with anise, yet so smoothly and softly powdered there are no "high" notes. The rose accord is there, but so gently honeyed with the barest musk, you have to play hide-and-seek to single it out. Almond is descernable, but certainly not predominant. Almond can be sharp, but I suppose the vanilla accord stops that tendency. And this vanilla is NOT the cake-y vanilla, either. It's an ethereal vanilla.

The dry-down is to die for. Softly floral, woody, yet still retaining baby-soft (not babyish) powder. I think "Instant" (I translate that to mean "the moment") is a misnomer for this Guerlain masterpiece. I would have named it "Denouement". I'm in love!

Czarcasm 03/23/14 12:02

Strong, heavy but sweet scent upon spraying it. I can smell a mixture of flowers and lemon. I find it a bit too strong at this point.

After the top notes have died down it has changed into a warm, sweet floral smell. It's also a bit powdery.

I like the drydown best. The smell is simply beautiful. I'm getting mostly vanilla with some iris. The first few times I tried it I was unable to distinguish the almond, but after wearing it a couple of times I'm now getting lots of almond.

I really like L'Instant Magic, the only downside is that the initial smell is a bit strong and therefore a little harsh on the nose. Beware of overspraying! You really only need about two sprays of this or it becomes too much! Also, you might not want to spray this onto (light-coloured) clothing, as it leaves stains.

It's a luxurious fragrance that I personally would wear at night time or cold/rainy days. It fills me with warmth, like I'm snuggling with a blanket in front of a smoldering fireplace. It took me a while to really get this fragrance but now that I do, I've really come to love it.

jæ 05/23/20 16:22

Yeah, I get why people associate this with baby powder, mineral oil, lotion, and laundry products. The violet, sweet almond, iris, and freesia notes occur in many other household items we want to associate with cleanliness, warmth, and comfort. To me, this is not a disqualifier. L'Instant magique is more complex than any of these products, and more nuanced.

At first, the powdery iris and violet dance with the bright citruses and anise, which provides an almost licorice-like harmony. Soon, that beautiful vanilla-almond accord starts to come through, along with a host of other florals, which are difficult to detect individually. The breezy, nectar-sweet freesia is definitely there, as is the soapy rose, and maybe a hint of mimosa in all its pollinated glory. The drydown leads to an almond-musk-violet haze with flashes of flowers and anise.

Taken together, this is supremely refreshing and sheer, but melds very well with skin and sweat. The performance is middling, but this is one of those fragrances that is difficult to over-apply. At worst, you're left smelling like you've just bathed in a tub full of luscious soaps and oils, followed by the application of a fine lotion or body oil.

I should also note that this review is for the bee bottle version; I've never smelled earlier formulations. Traditionally feminine, but I wish more guys smelled this good and clean, haha. All-season, but blooms better in warm weather. Merci, Guerlain!

Call off the search, spread the good news, this is what I want to smell like for the rest of my life! Thank you for coming to my TED talk.

Definitely a very nice makeup scent. The powder can feel a little strong on initial application but just bear with it because it does mellow out (at least on me). It's so beautiful and delicate and it just smells like something a fairy princess would wear. After a while the dry down becomes a little sweeter with the vanilla and almond which reminds me of when your mixing butter and powdered sugar and it gets in the air and you can smell the sweetness of the powdered sugar (if that makes sense to anyone). The florals stay dancing in the background and I hope that they never discontinue this because my heart will legitimately break.

It's a bonus that I personally really like the bee bottle design. I have never smelled the one in the old bottle so I can't compare, but if that was stronger, it's likely it would have been too strong for me.

Most Popular Negative Reviews

Scout 12/10/13 06:33

I'm going to be a bit more negative for this than other reviewers. My impression of this is one of personal preference. If you like this kind of scent, it must be overwhelmingly gorgeous for you. It is largely unpleasant for me, mainly because it is so overwhelmingly strong. The tone, the notes, the sweetness of this is fine enough. But it has an achingly overwhelming powdery projection. The sillage creeps into every crevice of your senses like fog rising into the space between trees in a forest, like steam accumulating in every open pore. It is STRONG, and could easily be offensive in a small space.
At first spray, it's light and is seemingly just a "thin veil" type of smell. But it develops and gets much much bigger over time. The scent compounds!
This is much more similar to My Insolence than I would have ever predicted. It has the same sweet synthetic feel and overwhelming construction, and the same sweet thick powdery vibe. The difference is that this is much more neutral and not "sour," if that description conjures up any helpful images for you.
I expected something a bit more nutty and warm, given the almond, vanilla, sandalwood,etc... Instead it's a wall of musk and sweet in a high-pitched shreik. This is the Lauder "Pleasures" of powdery smells. IMO it needs some depth, some grounding, but maybe that would be TOO oriental? I don't know...
And for what it's worth, both my husband and I got headaches the day I tested this. One spritz on my arm. That's it. He complained of having a sharp feeling against his skull (he didn't even know I had tested it), and then an hour later I got a similar stabbing feeling in the front of my head. Truly truly strong stuff.
